content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends; true prices often dip below forecast before rebounding.
- Forecasting horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is mixed or mildly positive.
- When sentiment turns negative mid-period, model fails to adjust downward quickly — true price often drops sharply.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts, especially when sentiment spikes then reverses — forecasts overshoot and then collapse.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high forecasts too long after recent peaks, ignoring momentum decay.
- Forecasting should reduce volatility in early days of negative sentiment, as true price often stabilizes or declines faster than model suggests.
